Name: Quantum Storage
Description:
[h2]Storage Relays[/h2]

Version 1.3.0 enables all ten Relay types through Tier 3 Quasi-Quantum Storage, after Improved Assembly. All Relays occupy one tile, use 10 kW and automatically link matching powered units within 12 tiles through walls. Capacity is fixed and additive: General Storage 250; Cabinet 150; Refrigerator 275; Freezer 275; Beverage Cooler 75; Pantry 1300; Weapons Locker 100; Wardrobe 100; Organ Storage 300; Part Storage 150 per unit.

Each Relay keeps its own native saved share. Power loss seals that share and breaks links; removal ejects only that unit's contents. Eject All empties the active connected chain at the selected unit. Material quantities and individual object records use one shared topology and allocation policy, with two Core adapters. Active reservations stay pinned. The 1.3.0 Relay family passed representative in-game build and connection testing and was published to the Workshop. The compatibility repair is retained in restart-tested version 1.3.3.

Construction uses the vanilla counterpart's basic recipe plus 1–2 Improved Microchips according to its highest Tier 1–3 research equivalent. Relays remain separate from advanced Quantum networks and do not receive extra Quantum object-Hive or TACC hauling integration.

[h2]Quantum Storage[/h2]

Quantum Storage adds ten compact late-game storage endpoints. Each endpoint connects to a shared pool reserved for its storage type. Items deposited through one unit are available through every matching unit. Initial capacity follows the scale of the corresponding vanilla storage. Each additional endpoint doubles the network total.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Isolated Storage Networks[/h3]
- Quantum Storage Unit accepts general raw materials
- Quantum Cabinet accepts upgrade modules
- Quantum Freezer and Quantum Fridge maintain separate networks for temperature-sensitive materials
- Quantum Beverage Cooler accepts drinks
- Quantum Pantry accepts inedible raw food
- Quantum Weapons Locker and Wardrobe store weapons and clothing
- Quantum Organ Storage and Parts Storage retain individual body-part records
- Each network maintains its own capacity and contents
- Urns continue to use Core's memorial-storage system

[h3]Shared Capacity[/h3]
- Every endpoint occupies one tile
- Each matching endpoint doubles the capacity of its network
- Non-final endpoint removal retains the shared contents
- An overfull network refuses new deposits until capacity becomes available
- Final endpoint removal ejects the contents through Core's storage process

[h3]Core Storage Integration[/h3]
- Stardeus remains responsible for filters and haul priorities
- Core continues to manage reservations and reachability
- Stored objects retain identity, quality, condition, and body-part state
- Matching endpoints provide shared access and item ejection

[h3]Research-Gated Nanobot Delivery[/h3]
- Nanobot Hives can deliver loose weapons and clothing to their matching Quantum storage
- Robotic parts become eligible after Basic Bot Parts research
- Organic parts become eligible after Basic Synthetic Organs research
- All four routes require Nanobots research and normal Hive coverage
- Destination power, capacity, priority, and filters remain authoritative
- Delivery is one-way; Hives do not extract stored objects
- A Hive can service floor replacement beneath a wall or door from an adjacent room
- A Quantum Storage Unit can supply the requested material through Core's normal source selection
- Core replacement tasks, reservations, Hive range, and room coverage remain authoritative
- The feature uses existing Core technologies

[h3]Optional TACC Integration[/h3]
- When TACC is installed, Nanobot Hives can carry washable clothing from Quantum Wardrobes to Washing Machines
- Hives can return clothing discharged by a Washing Machine to a Quantum Wardrobe
- Washing Machine settings, Quantum Wardrobe filters, reservations, Hive coverage, and ordinary hauling remain authoritative
- TACC is optional and is not required to load or use Quantum Storage

[h3]Power and Damage Feedback[/h3]
- Each powered endpoint consumes 25 kW
- Quantum material endpoints operate without Safe Area or ambient storage-temperature requirements
- Fire and explosion damage can transfer a small portion of the hit to one powered peer
- Transfer damage stays within the same network and cannot chain
- A Fuse installed at the source cancels one successful transfer event

[h2]Research[/h2]

Quantum Storage is a Tier 5 technology. It requires Quantum Computing and Storage. Nanobot object delivery becomes available through the relevant Core research. Optional TACC transfers use the existing Nanobots research gate.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Stardeus 0.15.0-rc341[/b] or later; reviewed against rc342.3224. Version 1.3.8 checks the resolved material-panel contract at startup, allowing harmless metadata renumbering while retaining native-panel fallback for unverified contracts. Future Core changes can still require compatibility review. Quantum Storage operates as a standalone mod. TACC support activates only when TACC is installed.

[h2]Summary[/h2]

Matching endpoints share capacity and contents. Separate storage types remain isolated.

[b]Shared access. Separate inventories.[/b]
